I am an old woman of 71 years, and this small plot of 0.29 hectares is rented land where I grow my yams and cassava together with some vegetables. Money is tight and the land is not mine, so I cannot spend too much on chemical fertilizer — I will buy a small bag of NPK to help the yams, but mostly I rely on the goat and chicken droppings I collect from my compound. My children and grandchildren help me with planting and weeding, so I manage most of the work with family hands, but for making the yam heaps at the start of the season my back cannot do it alone, so I must hire a young man for some days. I plant the yam setts I saved from last year's harvest and cassava cuttings from my neighbor — I do not bother with irrigation because the rains come well here in the South East.
